claims.claim: DOE's 2022 selectee record independently supports the existence of a large planned separator-localization program and Microvast's vertical-integration thesis, but it is not current evidence that the proposed 19 GWh separator facility reached completion, final award, utilization, contracted demand, or attractive economics.

causalEdges.from: localized separator and battery manufacturing capacity
causalEdges.to: supply-chain resilience and potential bottleneck control
causalEdges.mechanism: domestic materials/cell/pack integration can reduce external supply dependence if facilities are completed and economically utilized
causalEdges.falsifier: current primary evidence shows the proposed separator project was not completed/funded or remains materially underutilized

causalEdges.from: planned capacity without demonstrated contracted utilization
causalEdges.mechanism: capacity can add fixed-cost and capital burden before customer ramps create sufficient absorption
causalEdges.falsifier: current primary evidence demonstrates contracted utilization plus improving utilization/margin economics

risks: Historical planned capacity can inflate confidence if treated as present operating capacity, demand, backlog, pricing power, or return on invested capital.
Localization improves resilience only if project completion, qualification, customer adoption and utilization convert planned infrastructure into productive assets.
unknowns: Current completion/funding status of the DOE-described separator project.
Current utilization, contracted demand and unit economics associated with the planned separator capacity and Clarksville capacity.

gatingStatus.reason: This assist clarifies the evidentiary boundary around a historical primary source; it does not create a present blocker or Alpha numeric risk value.

confidence.basis: The boundary is directly supported by the DOE record's historical selectee/program nature and is consistent with the latest Scout assist; current project status remains explicitly unknown.

improvementPath: Use a current SEC filing, issuer project update, or DOE award/project-status record to verify completion, funding, utilization and economics before assigning current quantitative risk treatment.
